chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad bin Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

the supplication in the month of Ramadan, during every night you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, whose Hajj is accepted, their evil deeds expiated from them, their sins forgiven, their striving appreciated.'

And that You make, regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, during the Night of Predestination, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You prolong my life, and expand my sustenance, and make me among those by whom You help Your religion, and do not replace me with others.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite every night in Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on the 'decree that is not repelled' (al-qada' al-mahdum), linking nightly Ramadan devotion with the specific blessings of Laylat al-Qadr. It uniquely combines personal petitions for longevity and sustenance with a communal role, asking to be among those who attain accepted pilgrimage (Hajj al-Mabrur) and serve as instruments of divine victory for the faith.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Atiyya,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the supplication in a Month of Ramazan, during every night: ‘You should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> regarding what You<sup>azwj</sup> have Judged, and Measured out from the Ordained matters, regarding the Wise matters from the Determination which are neither returned, nor exchanged, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Write for me to be from the Pilgrims of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Sacred House, whose Hajj is Accepted from them, their wickedness having been expiated from them, their sins being Forgiven from them, their striving being Appreciated from them.

And, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Make, with regards to whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> Judged for me, and Measured out from the Ordained matters, regarding the Wise matters during the Night of Pre-destination, from the Judgements which are neither returned nor exchanged, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Prolong my life-span, and Expand upon me in my sustenance, and Make me to be from the ones by whom Your<sup>azwj</sup> Religion is helped by, and not Replace me with others’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Atiyyah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

every night in the month of Ramadan you should say this prayer. ‘O Allah, I appeal before You in the case of whatever You decide and measure of the inevitable issues of the matters of wisdom, of the destiny that does not change or alter, to list my name among those who perform Hajj of Your respected House, with virtuous Hajj, expatiated wickedness, forgiven sins and appreciated efforts.

O Allah, I appeal before You, in the case of whatever You decide and measure of the inevitable issues of the matters of wisdom, during the night of destiny, which does not change or alter, to grant me long life, increased sustenance, and take me in the service of Your religion and do not replace me with others.’”
